content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification:** deviation (IP — ownership of deliverables and Customer Data), targeted at the preferred position.

**What I found:**
- §13.5 (p0115–p0116) is the only ownership provision touching work product. It starts well for us — Developments created solely by Corio "shall be owned by Corio", Commerce One "hereby assigns all rights in and to such Developments to Corio", subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership — but it flips direction whenever Commerce One supports the Developments on an ongoing basis, in which case Commerce One "will retain all ownership rights", with no licence back to Corio. That is walk-away territory and also fails fallback.
- No licence to Commerce One IP embedded in the Developments (§§2.1–2.3, 12.3 cover only the Software/Source Code, and none is both royalty-free and irrevocable in the relevant respect).
- No Customer Data ownership or use-limitation anywhere (confirmed by section sweep and data/ownership searches; §§2.8, 12.3 only reserve Commerce One's Software and Source Code rights, which is acceptable).
- Ownership of jointly developed Software enhancements is left to future negotiation, so "no joint ownership" is not stated.

**Redline (validated, minimality gate passed):** deleted the ownership-reversal carve-out in §13.5; added the proviso that no IP is jointly owned to the retained enhancement-ownership sentence (so the retained mechanic does not contradict the new rule); and inserted one short §13.5.1 carrying the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence plus Corio's data ownership with Commerce One's licence limited to processing that data solely to provide the Software, MarketSite.net Service and Maintenance and Support. The existing assignment and pre-existing IP reservation were left untouched as already met.
